entries.punishment: Death, or imprisonment for life, and fine.
essentialIngredients: causing of death of a human being
act done with the intention of causing death, or intention/knowledge of causing such bodily injury as is likely/sufficient in ordinary course to cause death
the case does not fall within the exceptions reducing it to culpable homicide not amounting to murder
entries.notes: IPC 302 -> BNS 103 per sanhita-map.json. Distinguish from culpable homicide not amounting to murder; check applicability of exceptions before pleading.

entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to five years and fine (enhanced punishment applies in specified aggravated situations — verify sub-section against the Act).
essentialIngredients: death of a human being
death caused by a rash or negligent act of the accused
the act does not amount to culpable homicide
entries.notes: IPC 304A -> BNS 106(1). BNS restructured negligence-death provisions and added specific sub-sections (e.g. hit-and-run / registered medical practitioner). Confirm the exact sub-section and quantum against the bare Act before citing.

aliases: unnatural death of wife within seven years
entries.punishment: Imprisonment for a term not less than seven years but which may extend to imprisonment for life.
essentialIngredients: death of a woman caused by burns/bodily injury or otherwise than under normal circumstances
death within seven years of marriage
soon before death she was subjected to cruelty or harassment by husband or his relative
such cruelty or harassment was in connection with any demand for dowry
entries.notes: IPC 304B -> BNS 80. Frequently pleaded together with BNS 85 (cruelty). Presumption provisions live in the evidence law (BSA) — cross-check.

entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to ten years and fine; if hurt is caused, up to imprisonment for life (verify sub-section against the Act).
essentialIngredients: an act done by the accused
the act done with such intention or knowledge and under such circumstances that, if it caused death, it would amount to murder
the act was a step towards commission of the offence (more than mere preparation)
entries.notes: IPC 307 -> BNS 109. Enhanced limb where hurt actually caused; confirm quantum and sub-section.

entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to one year, or fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees, or both.
essentialIngredients: the accused voluntarily caused hurt (bodily pain, disease or infirmity) to another
intention or knowledge that the act was likely to cause hurt
entries.notes: IPC 323 -> BNS 115(2). Bailable & non-cognizable & compoundable — status decisive for how the matter proceeds; verify against the First Schedule equivalent.

entries.sectionTitle: Punishment for voluntarily causing grievous hurt
entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to seven years and fine.
essentialIngredients: the accused voluntarily caused hurt
the hurt is grievous within the statutory definition (e.g. fracture, permanent disfiguration, endangering life, etc.)
intention or knowledge to cause grievous hurt
entries.notes: IPC 325 -> BNS 117(2). Turn on the statutory definition of 'grievous' — confirm the injury falls within an enumerated clause before pleading.

entries.offenceName: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
entries.sectionTitle: Voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means
entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to the term specified in the Act, and fine (verify quantum and hurt/grievous-hurt limb).
essentialIngredients: voluntary causing of hurt or grievous hurt
by means of an instrument for shooting, stabbing or cutting, or any dangerous instrument/means
intention or knowledge of causing hurt
entries.notes: IPC 324 -> BNS 118(1). Old IPC 324 was made non-bailable/cognizable in practice; confirm current classification and the exact quantum for the hurt vs grievous-hurt limb.

entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to three years, or fine, or both (with enhanced provisions for repeat offenders — verify against the Act).
essentialIngredients: dishonest intention to take property
the property is movable
the property is taken out of the possession of another person
taken without that person's consent
moving of the property in order to such taking
entries.notes: IPC 379 -> BNS 303(2). BNS 303 also carries a distinct provision for petty theft / repeat offenders and community-service option — confirm sub-section applicable to the value and history.

entries.offenceName: Theft in a dwelling house etc.
entries.sectionTitle: Theft in a dwelling house, or means of transportation or place of worship, etc.
entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to seven years and fine.
essentialIngredients: all ingredients of theft (BNS 303)
committed in a building/tent/vessel used as a human dwelling, or a place of worship, or a means of transportation
entries.notes: IPC 380 -> BNS 305. Aggravated theft by locus; often charged with trespass — check whether trespass ingredients are also made out.

entries.punishment: Rigorous imprisonment which may extend to ten years and fine; if committed on a highway between sunset and sunrise, up to fourteen years (verify).
essentialIngredients: theft or extortion (robbery is aggravated theft or aggravated extortion)
in order to commit / while committing / in carrying away property, the offender voluntarily causes or attempts to cause death, hurt, or wrongful restraint, or fear thereof
entries.notes: IPC 392 -> BNS 309(4). Robbery vs dacoity turns on number of offenders (five or more => dacoity). Confirm the aggravated-locus/time limb before citing enhanced quantum.

entries.sectionTitle: Punishment for criminal breach of trust
entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to five years, or fine, or both.
essentialIngredients: the accused was entrusted with property or with dominion over property
the accused dishonestly misappropriated / converted to own use / used or disposed of that property in violation of a direction or of any legal contract
the property belonged to another
entries.notes: IPC 406 -> BNS 316(2). KEY DISTINCTION for the engine: cheating (318) requires deception AT INCEPTION; CBT (316) starts with lawful entrustment and later dishonesty. If property was handed over voluntarily on trust, look at 316 not 318.

entries.offenceName: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
entries.sectionTitle: Cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property
entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to seven years and fine.
essentialIngredients: deception of a person by the accused
fraudulent or dishonest inducement of that person
the person so induced delivered any property to any person, or made/altered/destroyed a valuable security
dishonest intention present at the time of the inducement
entries.notes: IPC 420 -> BNS 318(4). Engine check: was PROPERTY actually delivered? If deception but no delivery, it may be simple cheating (a lower limb of 318), not 318(4). If entrustment then dishonesty, consider 316 (CBT) instead.

entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to three months, or fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or both (verify — house-trespass limb is higher).
essentialIngredients: entry into or upon property in the possession of another
entry (or unlawful remaining after lawful entry) was with intent to commit an offence, or to intimidate, insult or annoy the person in possession
entries.notes: IPC 447 -> BNS 329(3). Note the distinct, heavier house-trespass limbs within the same cluster; confirm which limb the facts attract.

entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to the term specified in the applicable sub-section and fine (varies by type of document forged — verify).
essentialIngredients: making of a false document or false electronic record (or part thereof)
with intent to cause damage or injury, or to support a claim, or to cause a person to part with property, or to enter into a contract, or to commit fraud
entries.notes: IPC 463 -> BNS 336(1) per sanhita-map.json (forgery cluster). oldRef is 463 (the forgery definition/punishment cluster), NOT 420. Punishment quantum varies by the TYPE of document forged (e.g. court records, valuable security) — resolve the specific limb before citing quantum.

entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to two years, or fine, or both; aggravated limb (threat to cause death/grievous hurt etc.) up to seven years (verify sub-section).
essentialIngredients: a threat by the accused to another person
the threat is of injury to person, reputation or property of that person or of someone in whom he is interested
intent to cause alarm, or to cause the person to do/omit an act he is not legally bound to do/omit
entries.notes: IPC 506 -> BNS 351(2). Two limbs (simple vs aggravated); the aggravated limb is the one usually pleaded. Cognizability often depends on State notification — flag for advocate.

entries.offenceName: Cruelty by husband or relative of husband
entries.sectionTitle: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to three years and fine.
essentialIngredients: the woman is/was married to the accused (or accused is a relative of the husband)
the accused subjected her to cruelty
cruelty means wilful conduct likely to drive her to suicide or cause grave injury/danger, OR harassment to coerce an unlawful demand for property/valuable security
entries.notes: IPC 498A -> BNS 85. Definition of 'cruelty' sits in the neighbouring section (BNS 86); cite both when pleading. Non-compoundable in general — advise accordingly.

entries.offenceName: Assault or criminal force to woman with intent to outrage modesty
entries.sectionTitle: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
entries.punishment: Imprisonment for a term not less than one year which may extend to five years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: assault or use of criminal force by the accused to a woman
intention to outrage, or knowledge of likelihood of outraging, her modesty
entries.notes: IPC 354 -> BNS 74. Distinguish from BNS 79 (word/gesture — no physical force) and from graver sexual offences. Non-compoundable.

entries.offenceName: Word, gesture or act intended to insult modesty of a woman
entries.sectionTitle: Word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman
entries.punishment: Simple imprisonment which may extend to three years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: the accused uttered a word, made a sound/gesture, or exhibited an object, or intruded upon privacy
intent that it be heard/seen by the woman, intending to insult her modesty
entries.notes: IPC 509 -> BNS 79. No physical force — that is what separates it from BNS 74.

entries.punishment: Rigorous imprisonment not less than ten years, extendable to imprisonment for life, and fine (aggravated forms carry higher minimums — verify sub-section).
essentialIngredients: the act falls within the statutory definition of rape (BNS definition section)
absence of valid consent as defined by the Act
the woman/victim and circumstances fall within the section's scope
entries.notes: IPC 376 -> BNS 64. Sensitive offence: the DEFINITION of rape sits in a separate section (BNS 63) and consent provisions are technical. Engine must NOT auto-draft specifics; escalate to advocate. Special protections for victim identity (BNS/BSA) apply to the document itself.

entries.punishment: Imprisonment which may extend to seven years and fine.
essentialIngredients: kidnapping from India, or kidnapping from lawful guardianship (as defined)
for lawful-guardianship limb: taking/enticing a minor (under the specified age) or person of unsound mind out of the keeping of the lawful guardian without consent
entries.notes: IPC 363 -> BNS 137. Kidnapping (137) vs abduction (separate cluster) is a classic confusion — abduction requires force/deceit and is not itself punishable unless coupled with an aggravating intent. Confirm age thresholds against the Act.

entries.sectionTitle: Unlawful assembly (and punishment for being a member)
aliases: group of five or more common object
entries.punishment: Varies by sub-section/limb (membership vs rioting vs armed rioting) — verify each against the Act.
essentialIngredients: an assembly of five or more persons
a common object among them that is one of the unlawful objects enumerated in the Act
for rioting limbs: use of force or violence by the assembly or any member in prosecution of the common object
entries.notes: IPC 141/143/147/149 collapse into the BNS 189-191 cluster (see sanhita-map.json). This entry is a CLUSTER pointer; when charging, resolve to the specific sub-section (membership/rioting/armed/common-object vicarious liability).

entries.triableBy: Same as the offence which is the object of the conspiracy
entries.punishment: Where the object is an offence punishable with death/life/2+ years rigorous imprisonment: same as abetment of that offence; otherwise up to six months, or fine, or both (verify).
essentialIngredients: an agreement between two or more persons
to do, or cause to be done, an illegal act, or a legal act by illegal means
for offences not punishable as above, some act besides the agreement done in pursuance of it
entries.notes: IPC 120A/120B -> BNS 61(1)/(2). Bailability/cognizability and forum FOLLOW the object offence — the engine must resolve those from the substantive charge, not from this entry in isolation.
